# Patches to the vendored Ghidra decompiler

Applied on top of Ghidra 12.3 (`918d44e`) by `../vendor.py`, in file-name order, with
`git apply --check` first so that a patch which no longer applies stops the vendoring step
instead of being skipped. The files under `../cpp/` are never edited by hand: a change to
the engine is a new numbered patch here, with a reason in this table and a test that fails
without it.

Each patched file also gets a one-line "Modified for SaturnExplorer" notice in its licence
header, because Apache-2.0 §4(b) asks modified files to say so.

| Patch | Why | Pinned by |
|---|---|---|
| `0001-cancel-flag.patch` | The bare library has no cancellation hook (Ghidra cancels by killing its decompiler process). Adds a host-owned `std::atomic<bool>*` on `Architecture` and `CancelError` check-points in `FlowInfo::fallthru` (per instruction, so every worklist loop and straight-line run), the jump-table loop of `FlowInfo::generateOps`, `Action::perform` (every action, every level) and `ActionPool::apply` (every 1024 ops); and makes `Funcdata::stageJumpTable` rethrow `CancelError` instead of treating it as a failed jump-table recovery, which swallowed a cancel raised inside the nested "jumptable" simplification. 25 functional lines in 6 files, plus the notices. Cooperative: `Architecture` construction, the body of one action, printing and teardown have no check-point. The spike's `Docs/Decompiler/spike/patches/0001-cancel-flag.patch` plus the `stageJumpTable` rethrow (found in review), the notices, and `CancelError` placed before `RecovError`'s doc comment instead of inside it. | `Sh2DecompilerEngineTests` (`TestCancelDuringJumpTableRecovery`: a cancel requested from inside jump-table simplification must reach the host); `Docs/Decompiler/spike/cancel_spike.cpp`; `DecompilerRunnerTests` from Step 2 |
| `0002-sleigh-reset-null-caches.patch` | `Sleigh::reset` deletes the translator's context and disassembly caches (`clearForDelete`) and then allocates their replacements. If that allocation fails, the deleted pointers stay in the translator, which is a process-global object owned by `SleighArchitecture`'s static map: refusing all later requests (the host's policy after an engine-side out-of-memory) cannot stop its destructor from deleting them again at exit, and the process ended in `free(): double free` (found in the Step 2 review). `clearForDelete` now nulls both pointers after deleting them; `delete` of null is a no-op, so nothing else changes. 2 functional lines in 1 file, plus the notice. | `Sh2DecompilerTests` and `DecompilerRunnerTests` reset-OOM children: an allocation in `Sleigh::reset` fails, later requests are refused, and the process must then exit normally through static destruction |
| `0003-translator-ownership-on-init-failure.patch` | `Architecture::restoreFromSpec` held the new translator in a `unique_ptr` until `initialize()` returned. For a `SleighArchitecture` the translator is not the Architecture's: it is the process-global one in `SleighArchitecture`'s static map, reused by every Architecture. An allocation failure in `initialize()` on that reused translator (`reregisterContext`, its new disassembly cache) made the `unique_ptr` delete the map's object (`free(): invalid pointer`, found while testing 0002). The translator is now assigned to `translate` before `initialize()`, so it is owned by each Architecture's existing rules: a plain `Architecture` deletes it, and `SleighArchitecture`'s destructor clears `translate` first. 3 functional lines in 1 file, plus the notice. | `Sh2DecompilerTests` reset-OOM child with the failure one allocation later, inside `Sleigh::initialize`: the process must exit normally |
| `0004-funcdata-frees-active-output.patch` | `ActionPrototypeTypes` allocates a `ParamActive` (`Funcdata::initActiveOutput`) that return recovery frees when it completes. `Funcdata::~Funcdata` did not free it, so an analysis abandoned in between -- which the host's cancellation (0001) does, e.g. whenever the SH-2 Pseudocode panel supersedes a request -- leaked one (~48 bytes) per cancel; LeakSanitizer reported it in `DecompilerRunnerTests` whenever the cancel landed there (found in Step 3's review). The destructor now calls `clearActiveOutput()`, which deletes it if present and is a no-op otherwise. 1 functional line in 1 file, plus the notice. | `Sh2DecompilerTests` (`TestFunctionFreesActiveOutput`: creates the state directly, watches its allocation through the test allocator, destroys the Architecture, and requires it freed -- no dependence on where a cancel lands) |
